newsitem.title: UK: U.S. firms set up Mondex cash card franchise.
newsitem.headline: U.S. firms set up Mondex cash card franchise.

text.p: A group of seven U.S. companies on Thursday said they had established a company to develop and implement the U.S. franchise of international electronic cash system Mondex.

The company, Mondex USA Services, was set up by AT & T, through AT & T Universal Card Services, Chase Manhattan, Dean Witter Discover, First Chicago NBD, payments company Mastercard, Michigan National Bank and Wells Fargo.

Mastercard announced last month it would take a 51 pecent stake in Mastercard International which oversees global branding, technology development, security and risk management and the sale of Mondex licences to non-equity countries where the franchise has not already been purchased.
It was established in July and is owned by 17 founding companies including National Westminster Bank, Royal Bank of Canada, HSBC and 10 major banks in Australia and New Zealand.

"The stature and experience of all these insitiutions who are backing Mondex (USA) offer further evidence that Mondex will be the global standard for chip-based payment products," said Janet Hartung Crane, president and CEO of Mondex USA said.
Mondex allows consumers to store "electronic cash" on a smart card with an embedded microprocessor.
They can use the card to make small "cash" purchases at stores and over the Internet, having loaded cash via the telephone or a PC or from public locations like shops from cashless ATMs.
Merchants will reduce cash handling costs and be able to make electronic cash deposits.

Mondex USA said the system will allow Internet commerce to expand rapidly by introducing a cash option to on-line transaction and the multi-use card will also offer loyalty programme facilities and personal identification applications. -- Joe Ortiz, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717.
